document.title: New Fighting and New Forces in Kandahar
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Consular officials report on a stranded Pakistani aid convoy and fighting between Afghan factions in Kandahar. One party is a new movement, the Taliban ("Seekers"), which had taken Spin Boldak and came from madrasas in Quetta and Peshawar. Speculation about who supports Mullah Omar's Taliban is rife. The movement may be a new phenomenon independent of party politics. Excised.

events.description: A new group using the Taliban name surfaced in Kandahar Province under Mullah Mohammad Omar and deputy Ehsanullah.
The Taliban captured Mullah Fatah Mohammad after a short firefight, tried him by summary shariat trial and hanged him for brigandage.
Taliban campaign began, clearing freelance checkposts between Kandahar and the border, with tacit initial approval of Gul Agha.
Taliban occupied Spin Boldak from HIG after a night attack begun 12 Oct; five HIG and three Taliban reportedly died.
Taliban deputy Ehsanullah's BBC interview (14/15 Oct) said goals were to eliminate Wahabi/Salafi influence and open the highway; supported the Mestiri process and a loya jirga.
Pakistani aid/trade convoy was originally scheduled to enter Afghanistan but was held up by Taliban objections at Spin Boldak.
Convoy with Taliban members and Pakistani consul Iman passed through Spin Boldak without incident, then was stopped south of Kandahar by Gul Agha, Lalai and Mansur's troops.
Forces of Sar Kateb, Gul Agha, Lalai and Mansur attacked Taliban-held Takht-e Pul; repulsed, as was a follow-up on Wednesday 2 Nov.
Taliban attacked and took two hilltop positions of Sar Kateb near Bara Pul.
Mullah Yar Mohammed's troops reportedly left Arghistan to attack the commanders' alliance from the rear in support of the Taliban.
UN envoy Mestiri's scheduled Kandahar visit cancelled because of the fighting.
HIG/NIFA commanders attacked Taliban-held Takht-e Pul; repulsed, with a follow-up attack repulsed on Wednesday.
Follow-up attack on Takht-e Pul repulsed.
Mullah Yar Mohammed's troops left Arghistan to attack the commanders' alliance from the rear.
Pakistani aid convoy originally scheduled to enter Afghanistan, delayed due to Taliban objections at Spin Boldak.
Taliban spokesman Mullah Mohammad Ghaus set conditions for the convoy's entry into Afghanistan.
Taliban begin campaign clearing free-lance checkposts between Kandahar and the border.
Taliban begin night attack on Spin Boldak.
Taliban occupy Spin Boldak; reportedly five HIG and three Taliban dead.
Ehsanullah's BBC interview (Oct 14/15) on eliminating Wahabi influence and opening the highway.
Troops of Gul Agha, Lalai and Mansur stopped the convoy south of Kandahar; drivers roughed up.
Taliban summarily tried and hanged Mullah Fatah Mohammad for brigandage after refusing to open the road.
New Taliban group surfaced in Kandahar Province under Mullah Omar.
Mestiri's scheduled visit to Kandahar cancelled owing to fighting.

key_claims: The new Taliban, led by Mullah Mohammad Omar, emerged in early summer 1994 in Kandahar, mostly from young religious students who had not fought in the jihad.
The Taliban took Spin Boldak from HIG on 13 Oct 1994 and delayed the first Pakistani convoy to Central Asia, then fought Gul Agha, Lalai, Mansur and Sar Kateb around Kandahar.
Many suspect Pakistan, via Interior Minister Babar and Fazl Rehman's JUI madrasa recruiting, of backing the Taliban, but the Taliban claim independence.
Some sources claim the Taliban are surrogates of Rabbani or Sayyaf, and others say Sayyaf stage-managed the opposition via Capt Musa.
